findings.claim: Writing `at: today` as a bare date does not clear a concept or docs page whose source changed today. as_datetime reads a bare date as its UTC midnight, and review_due flags `source changed` when the source's last commit time is later than verified_at. So a person who checks a concept the same day its source changed runs kmctl verify, gets exit 0, and the id is still listed. That breaks the plan's core promise (the id leaves kmctl review due). For a docs page it is the common case, since a docs page is never due for `unverified`, only for stale_after or a changed source. The plan should write a full UTC datetime (OKF dates are ISO 8601 datetimes since v0.2, and generated.at already uses them), and r1/r2 should include a source committed earlier the same day.

A verified entry does not clear the `stale_after passed` reason, yet the plan's new Next: line in kmctl review due points at kmctl verify whenever anything is due, and the done-when says verify makes review due stop listing the id. An agent sent by that line to verify a concept or docs page that is due for stale_after runs the verb and the id stays due. That is the same dead end the operator reported. The plan has to choose: verify also moves or clears stale_after (one more input and its rule), or the Next: line and the verb's help say verify clears only `unverified` and `source changed`, and name the fix for stale_after. r6 and r1/r2 should test whichever is chosen.
